claims.text: Heterogeneous lattice strain causes unusual dislocation behaviors, including multiple kinks, jogs, and bidirectional cross-slip.
There is an optimal level of heterogeneous lattice strain for retaining toughness.
Lattice-strain-induced dislocation behaviors facilitate the nucleation of nano-twin boundaries.
Lattice-strain-induced dislocation behaviors facilitate effective migration of nano-twin boundaries.
Nano-twin boundaries act as barriers that deflect or impede crack propagation.
Nano-twinning can help retain toughness by providing an additional deformation mode.
Reducing atomic-size mismatch reduces heterogeneous lattice strain.
Reducing heterogeneous lattice strain decreases beneficial dislocation events and nano-twin density.
Reducing heterogeneous lattice strain decreases fracture toughness relative to the optimized baseline.
Excessive heterogeneous lattice strain decreases the density or effectiveness of nano-twin boundaries.
Overshooting the optimal heterogeneous lattice strain causes toughness loss.
Heterogeneous lattice strain can underpin strength-ductility synergy through dislocation-mediated strengthening.
The proposed baseline is a previously optimized composition having high fracture toughness and strength-ductility synergy.
Nano-twinning contributes to simultaneous strength, ductility, and toughness enhancement between room and cryogenic temperatures.
The complete lattice-strain-to-dislocation-to-nano-twin toughness mechanism should hold in distorted FCC high-entropy alloys at moderate temperatures and engineering-relevant strain rates.
Phase transformations or secondary-phase precipitation may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
Systematically varying the concentration of a large-size-mismatch element is the proposed controlled intervention for changing lattice-strain heterogeneity.
The exact lattice-strain and nano-twin-density thresholds for maximum toughness are uncertain and may depend on alloy system and processing.
Failure of lattice-strain changes to produce corresponding nano-twin-density and toughness trends would falsify the proposed mediation mechanism.
